question.problem:
$$

Which of the following is equivalent to $\operatorname{arsinh}⁡(\frac{{t}^{2}-1}{2t}),$ for $t>0?$
question.worked_solution:
The definition of $\operatorname{arsinh}⁡x$ is 

$$
\operatorname{arsinh}⁡x=\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+\sqrt{{x}^{2}+1}).
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{arsinh}⁡(\frac{{t}^{2}-1}{2t}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{{t}^{2}-1}{2t}+\sqrt{{(\frac{{t}^{2}-1}{2t})}^{2}+1}) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{{t}^{2}-1}{2t}+\sqrt{\frac{{t}^{4}-2{t}^{2}+1}{4{t}^{2}}+1}) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{{t}^{2}-1}{2t}+\sqrt{\frac{{t}^{4}+2{t}^{2}+1}{4{t}^{2}}}) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{{t}^{2}-1}{2t}+\sqrt{{(\frac{{t}^{2}+1}{2t})}^{2}}) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{{t}^{2}-1}{2t}+|\frac{{t}^{2}+1}{2t}|)\end{aligned}
$$

Since $t>0,$ we have $\frac{{t}^{2}+1}{2t}>0,$ and we can remove the absolute value in the above expression. Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{arsinh}⁡(\frac{{t}^{2}-1}{2t}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{{t}^{2}-1}{2t}+\frac{{t}^{2}+1}{2t}) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{2{t}^{2}}{2t}) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡t.\end{aligned}
$$
